text: I'm trying to decide whether to repaint the kids' rooms myself or hire someone. Two rooms, about twelve by twelve each, and one of them has a dark purple accent wall from the previous owners that's going to need primer. A painter quoted eleven hundred for both. I could probably do it for two hundred in supplies, but it would take me three weekends and my back is already complaining. My oldest wants her room to be sage green now because she saw it on some video, and my youngest wants it to stay the exact same blue because he says changing it would be weird. So really it's one room. That cuts the quote down, I guess, unless the purple wall counts as its own project.

So my sister Dana called this morning and said the twins' birthday party got moved from Saturday to Sunday the fourteenth because the bounce house place double booked them. She wants everyone at the park pavilion by eleven thirty, and she said Aunt Ruth is bringing the cake this time instead of ordering one from Costco. Honestly I think that's a mistake because Ruth's frosting always melts in the sun, but I'm not going to be the one to tell her that.

Set an alarm for five fifteen tomorrow morning because I have to get Ellie to the airport for her seven a.m. flight to Denver and you know she's never packed the night before, she'll be throwing socks in a duffel at five thirty while I'm sitting in the car honking.

I had the strangest conversation with our neighbor Mr. Okafor today. He's lived on this street since 1979 and he told me the whole cul-de-sac used to be an apple orchard, and that there's still one original tree in the Hendersons' backyard. He said the farmer's name was Lyle Brandt and he sold the land in pieces to pay for his daughter's college. I had no idea. It kind of changes how I see the street. He also said there used to be a creek running behind our house, before they put in the storm drains in the eighties. That explains why our basement floods every April. I always thought it was just bad luck. Turns out we bought a house on top of a creek.

Honestly I'm a little worried about my dad. He got lost driving home from the barber shop last week, a route he's driven for thirty years, and my mom only told me yesterday. He laughed it off and said he was distracted. But my mom said it's the second time this month. I want to bring it up at his next doctor's appointment, which I think is in early December, but I don't want him to feel like we're ganging up on him. How do families usually start that conversation?

So my daughter's science fair project is on whether music affects how fast plants grow. She's got three bean plants, one with classical, one with heavy metal, one with nothing. After two weeks the classical one is eleven centimeters, the metal one is nine, and the quiet one is ten. I told her that's probably just noise, not a real result, but she's convinced Mozart is magic. Is there any real research on that? She's also decided she wants to add a fourth plant that gets country music, and my husband said absolutely not because he refuses to listen to that through the vent for two more weeks. The fair is on the eighteenth, and the poster board alone has eaten our entire dining room table.

So I'm on my lunch walk and I just have to talk this through. My daughter Imani got into both colleges she wanted, Spelman and Howard, which is amazing, but the aid packages are really different. Spelman gave her twenty-two thousand a year in grants and Howard gave her about fourteen plus a work study. Howard is closer to her grandmother in Silver Spring though, so she'd have family nearby for holidays and emergencies. She has to decide by May first. I don't want to push her either way, I just want her to see the whole picture, the money, the distance, the vibe of each campus. When we visited Howard she lit up in a way I haven't seen in a while. But twenty-two versus fourteen is thirty-two thousand over four years. That's real money for us.

um I'm on the treadmill and I'm thinking about my grandfather's watch which my dad gave me before he died it's a 1962 Omega and it stopped working last year and a repair shop in town quoted me four hundred to service it which feels like a lot but it's the only thing I have of his honestly it's not about the money is it

My brother texted that he finally sold his landscaping business. He started it in 2006 with one truck and a used mower, and now he's got eleven employees and three trucks, and he sold it for a number he won't tell me but he said he's going to pay off the house and take his wife to Italy. I'm really happy for him. He worked six days a week for almost twenty years. I remember when he used to come over for Sunday dinner in his work boots with grass stuck all over him and my mom made him eat on the porch. Now he's going to Tuscany. Dad would have been so proud of him. He always said Tommy would figure it out his own way.

My grandmother turned ninety-two today and we did a little party at her assisted living place. She told the same story she always tells, about meeting my grandfather at a dance hall in Scranton in 1951 when he stepped on her foot and wouldn't stop apologizing. Then she wore his old cardigan the whole afternoon. I need to remember to call her more than once a week. She's not going to be around forever, and I keep acting like she will.

What's the difference between baking soda and baking powder? My son just asked me while we were making pancakes and I realized I honestly don't know, I just follow the recipe. He's nine and he wants a real answer, not just because the box says so, and honestly so do I at this point.

my youngest asked me today why the sky is blue and I gave him the whole speech about light scattering and he just looked at me and said no but why and I didn't have anything after that so what is the actual next level answer like for a seven year old who wont accept the first answer and then he asked why sunsets are orange and why clouds are white and at that point I just told him to ask his teacher which I know is a total cop out but I was also trying to merge onto the highway

Is it normal for a nine month old to not be crawling yet? My son Felix just kind of scoots on his butt and gets everywhere that way. His sister was crawling at seven months. The pediatrician appointment isn't until December and I'm trying not to Google it at midnight. He's pulling up on the couch, though, and he babbles constantly, so I think he's just doing it his own way. My mother-in-law says my husband didn't crawl either, he just stood up one day and walked at eleven months. Still, I'm a worrier.

Ugh. I left the lunch boxes on the counter again. Both of them. Zoe's has the strawberries she specifically asked for. I'm not turning around, we're already late. I really have to remember to put them by the door the night before. The school will give them the cafeteria pizza, they'll survive. This is the third time this month. Last week it was Zoe's library book and the week before that it was Caleb's cleats on game day. My husband says I take on too much in the mornings and he's right, but he also leaves at six fifteen, so who else is going to do it. Maybe the kids need to start packing their own bags. Zoe is eight, she can handle a lunch box.

I'm walking the dog and trying to plan out the meals for the week in my head. Monday is tacos because it's always tacos. Tuesday the kids have practice so something in the slow cooker, maybe that salsa chicken. Wednesday is leftovers. Thursday I want to try that sheet pan gnocchi everyone's posting about. Friday is pizza night. Saturday we're at the Martins'. Sunday I'll do a roast if I'm feeling ambitious, which I won't be. Honestly the hardest part isn't cooking, it's deciding. By Wednesday I just want someone to tell me what we're eating. The kids would eat chicken nuggets every night if I let them, and my husband would eat cereal. I'm the only one in this house who cares about vegetables and I'm losing.

I'm sitting in the pickup line at the high school and I'm watching all these kids come out and I swear half of them are taller than me. My son Ravi got his learner's permit last week and now he wants to drive everywhere, including the four minutes to his friend's house. He's actually pretty careful, but he brakes like the car owes him money. The driving school wants six hundred for the full course, and our insurance guy said adding him is going to cost about a hundred and ninety a month. A hundred and ninety. For a kid who still can't remember to put his dishes in the sink.

I was watching my youngest at gymnastics today and the coach said she's ready to move up to level three, which means practices go from one hour to two hours, twice a week, and the fee jumps from ninety to a hundred and sixty a month. She's six. I love that she loves it, but two hours on a weeknight at six years old feels like a lot. My husband did competitive swimming growing up and he says it burned him out by thirteen.

So I was clearing out my inbox and I saw that the confirmation for the Disney trip says we land in Orlando at two fifteen on March twelfth and check in at Pop Century, and our park reservations are Magic Kingdom the thirteenth, Hollywood Studios the fourteenth, and Animal Kingdom the fifteenth. The kids don't know yet. We're telling them on Christmas morning with a little treasure hunt. I'm so excited I can barely stand it. I already bought the little Mickey ears and wrapped them. My mom is coming too, and she's going to need a scooter for the long days, so I'll have to rent one there. It's the first time we've ever done anything this big. I've been saving for it since 2023 in a separate account the kids don't know about.

my wife and I have been arguing about the thermostat for literally eleven years she wants seventy four I want sixty eight and we compromised at seventy one but then I find it at seventy five every morning and she says she doesn't know how it got there I'm just saying there's a pattern and honestly the electric bill last month was two hundred and eighty dollars which is the highest it's ever been and she says it's because I take long showers and I say it's because the house is a sauna and the kids are sleeping on top of their blankets in November so you tell me who's right

We had the Okonkwo family over for dinner tonight and their youngest, Chidi, is allergic to eggs and dairy, so I made a whole vegan lasagna with cashew ricotta. It took me two hours. Their kid ate three bites and then had a peanut butter sandwich his mom brought. Everyone else loved it though, and my own kids didn't notice it was vegan until I told them, which was the best part of my night. I'm calling that a win.

Remember when we used to drive up to Tahoe every Presidents' Day weekend and stay at that motel with the broken ice machine? The kids are too old for it now, they want to go to the city instead. I miss those trips.

I've been thinking about starting a vegetable garden next spring, and I'm trying to decide between raised beds or just tilling a patch of the yard. The yard has a lot of clay, we're in Georgia, and the sunny spot is right by the fence where the dog likes to dig. Raised beds would be about three hundred dollars for lumber and soil. What vegetables are actually easy for a total beginner with three kids who will probably lose interest by July?

I think I'm going to sign up for that pottery class at the community center. It's Tuesday nights from six thirty to eight thirty, eight weeks, and it's a hundred and sixty five including clay and firing. My therapist said I need something with my hands that isn't my phone. The instructor is a retired art teacher named Gwen who apparently has a kiln in her garage. My sister took it last year and made a lopsided bowl that she uses for keys, and she said it was the best two hours of her week. My husband said he'd do bedtime on Tuesdays, which is generous considering he's never done bath time alone with all three of them. We'll see how that goes.

I have a weird question. Why do I always get a headache on Sunday afternoons? I sleep in, I have my coffee late, and by two o'clock I feel like garbage. My husband thinks it's caffeine withdrawal from not having my usual seven a.m. cup.

okay so um I just left the vet and they said Biscuit has a mild ear infection and the drops are twice a day for ten days and the bill was like two hundred and forty dollars which is insane for a dog who rolled in something gross at the creek I really need to remember to keep him on the leash near the water from now on and the vet tech said he might need a cone if he keeps scratching and he looked so sad when she said cone like he understood and my daughter wants to decorate it with stickers so he doesn't feel embarrassed which is the sweetest thing she's ever said about that dog

okay um so the realtor said the house on Birchwood is listed at four eighty five but they've had it on the market for sixty three days so we could probably offer four sixty and the inspection said the roof has maybe five years left and the HVAC is from 2009 so I'm thinking four fifty five with a credit for the roof but my husband thinks we'll lose it if we go that low what do you think is reasonable

I need to figure out how to explain to my five year old that Grandma's dog Rusty died. He loved that dog. Every time we visited, he'd throw the tennis ball for like an hour. Grandma said Rusty was fourteen and just went to sleep. I don't want to say "went to sleep" because I've read that can make kids scared of bedtime. How do people usually handle this at that age? He's already asking when we're going to Grandma's again so he can see Rusty. We're supposed to go on Saturday. Grandma said she's keeping his tennis ball by the back door, and I'm worried that's going to make it harder for him. Or maybe easier. I genuinely don't know.

My manager told me today that the quarterly review got pushed to December third and that I'll be presenting the warehouse throughput numbers, which are down about six percent from last quarter. I'm not panicking yet. The dip is mostly the forklift that was out of service for two weeks, and I have the maintenance logs to prove it. I just need to frame it right so it doesn't look like my team slacked off.

I'm trying to remember the name of that actor who was in the movie about the dog that waited at the train station. Richard something? It's going to bug me all day. My mom and I were trying to think of it at dinner and we both gave up and changed the subject.

I was talking to my friend Alana who runs a daycare out of her house and she said she's licensed for eight kids but she only takes six because she wants to actually give them attention. She charges two hundred and ten a week, which is cheaper than the centers around here. She has an opening in February. I'm not sure we're ready to switch Eli though, he just got comfortable where he is. He finally stopped crying at drop off in October, and his teacher Ms. Gloria says he's started talking way more. Switching would mean starting all over. But we'd save about eighty dollars a week, which over a year is serious money. I hate when the right choice for the budget isn't obviously the right choice for the kid.

Okay, quick question while I'm folding laundry. Is it actually bad to wash towels with regular clothes? My husband insists towels need their own load because of lint, but we're a family of six and I do like nine loads a week already. If I can combine anything at all, I'm doing it. My mom always washed everything together and our towels were fine, so I think this is a my-husband thing, not a laundry thing. He also folds his towels in thirds, which nobody else in the house does, and he refolds mine when he thinks I'm not looking.
um what's a good way to get tomato sauce out of a white shirt asking for a friend who is me and the friend has a parent teacher conference in an hour and the shirt was the only clean one

The roofer said the leak over the kids' bathroom is from the flashing around the vent pipe, not the shingles, so it's a three hundred dollar fix instead of a whole roof. I almost cried in relief. I'd been bracing for twelve grand since the water stain showed up. Sometimes things actually go right. He's coming back Thursday morning to fix it, and he even said he'd take a look at the gutters while he's up there for no charge. His name is Earl and he's been doing roofs in this town for thirty-one years. My neighbor recommended him, and I'm going to buy her a bottle of wine for it.

My boss pulled me aside today and said there might be a promotion to team lead opening up in Q2, but she said I need to show more visibility, whatever that means. She mentioned presenting at the all-hands in February. I hate public speaking. Last time I presented I said "um" probably sixty times. I think I'm going to do it anyway because the raise would be about eight percent and we really need it with the baby coming.

um so the HOA lady came by again about our trash cans being visible from the street and I told her we're building a little enclosure but honestly we haven't even started and the next meeting is the twentieth so I guess I'm building it this weekend whether I like it or not and I don't even own a miter saw so I'm going to have to borrow my neighbor Phil's and he's going to want to help which means it takes twice as long and involves a lot of opinions about wood stain and also somehow a beer at ten in the morning

okay this is random but what's the best way to get a toddler to eat vegetables because I've tried hiding them in smoothies and my son can taste spinach from across the room he's like a bloodhound for green things

My doctor said my cholesterol is two thirty-eight, which is up from two ten last year, and she wants me to recheck in six months before we talk about medication. She said cut back on red meat and get more walking in. I'm thinking I'll do the loop around Miller Pond every evening after dinner. It's about two point two miles. My wife said she'd come with me most nights, which helps. My dad had his first heart attack at fifty-three, so I'm taking it a little more seriously than I would have five years ago. I'm forty-nine now. My kids are still in middle school. I want to be around for a long time, and I want to be able to do things with them, not watch from a bench.

Okay, quick thing. My son's orthodontist, Dr. Feld, said Aiden needs a palate expander before braces, and the whole treatment is going to be about sixty-two hundred over two years. Insurance covers fifteen hundred lifetime. I need to remember to ask HR whether our plan resets in January because if it does maybe we wait. I'll call them Monday. Aiden is already self-conscious about his teeth because a kid on the bus said something, so I don't want to wait too long either. Dr. Feld said the expander phase is about six months and it can make him lisp a little at first. Aiden heard that part and now he's convinced everyone is going to laugh at him. Poor kid.

um so my mother keeps calling me about the family reunion in Branson next July and she wants a headcount by January and I keep telling her I don't know yet because Kevin's work schedule isn't out and she keeps saying just guess and I'm like Mom if I guess you're going to hold me to it like you did with the cruise in 2019

I need to remember to tell Josh that the carpool switch is happening next week. He has Monday and Wednesday, I have Tuesday and Thursday, and Fridays we're alternating starting with him. If I don't tell him in person he's not going to read the group chat. He never reads the group chat. Last time we changed the schedule he showed up on my day and we both sat in the pickup line waiting for the same three kids. The teachers thought it was hilarious. His wife says she'll remind him too, but she's traveling for work all next week, so it's really on me. I'll catch him at the bus stop Monday.

So the guy from the solar company came out and said we'd need about twenty two panels for our usage and it would be around twenty-six thousand before the tax credit, maybe eighteen after. He said payback is like nine years. We're probably moving in six or seven though, so I don't know if it makes sense. Does solar actually add to home value or is that sales talk? He also kept saying the offer was only good through the end of the month, which always makes me suspicious. My buddy Craig put panels on his house in Tempe and says his bill went to almost nothing in the summer. But we're in Ohio, it's cloudy half the year. I'll probably get two more quotes before I even think about it.

I keep thinking about whether we should put Maya in the Spanish immersion program at Lincoln or keep her at the neighborhood school. The immersion school is twenty minutes farther and there's no bus, so that's forty extra minutes of driving every day for me or Chris. But she loves languages and her teacher said she picks things up fast. I don't know. What do people usually weigh when they make a call like that?

Send a text to the group thread for the book club that I'm going to miss Thursday because of Henry's band concert. And tell them I loved the ending, even though Margaret's going to say it was predictable. She says that about every book.

You know what I was thinking about on the drive in? That summer we rented the cabin at Lake Winnipesaukee when the kids were tiny and Owen caught that sunfish and refused to let it go. He carried the bucket around for three hours. Remember that trip? I swear that was the best week we ever had as a family, before soccer took over every weekend.

so the parent group at Lily's school is organizing a holiday gift for the teachers and they want twenty five dollars per family which is fine but last year they also did one for the aides and the bus driver and that was another fifteen each and with three kids in the same school that adds up fast I'm not complaining exactly I just wish they'd combine it into one ask and then there's the sign up for the classroom party and the hat and mitten drive and the Thanksgiving canned food thing and every one of those emails comes with a little guilt trip at the bottom like we're hoping for one hundred percent participation from our families

I think it was Rachel who told me the swim lessons at the Y fill up within an hour of registration opening, so I've got to be on it at nine sharp on the second. Last session we missed out and Sam ended up in the Saturday seven a.m. slot, which was brutal for everybody. I'm writing myself a sticky note when I get home.

honestly I don't even know why I'm telling you this but Coach Ramirez benched Tyler for the whole second half today and he didn't say why and Tyler came home and went straight to his room and wouldn't talk and I'm trying to decide if I should email the coach or let it go because he's fourteen and maybe he needs to handle it himself

okay so how long should I boil eggs if I want them jammy in the middle like the ramen place because I keep getting either chalky or straight up raw and my daughter has very strong opinions about it like she will send them back

I forgot to pay the water bill again, that's the second month in a row. They sent the pink notice. I swear I need to set up autopay, I keep meaning to do it. Anyway it's only sixty-three dollars, I'll just pay it online when I get home tonight.

So my neighbor told me the city is putting in a new crosswalk at Fifth and Maple in the spring, and they're also adding a crossing guard at the middle school starting January. Which is great, because the morning traffic there is terrifying. Half the parents just drop their kids in the middle of the street. I'm glad someone finally complained loudly enough. The kids on our street have been crossing Maple to get to the bus stop for years and there's a blind curve right before it. My neighbor, Mrs. Alvarez, has been going to every city council meeting since June with a little binder of photos. She deserves a plaque. I should bake her something.

How long does cooked rice last in the fridge before it gets sketchy? I made a huge pot on Sunday for the stir fry and there's still like half of it left. My husband says rice is fine for a week and my mom says throw it out after a day, and they both say it with total confidence.

So I finally got the results back from that ancestry test. Turns out we're like thirty percent Irish, which my dad will be thrilled about, and there's eight percent Norwegian which nobody saw coming. And there's a second cousin match named Kristin Halvorsen who lives in Minnesota. I might reach out to her. My mom always said there was a branch of the family that went west after the war and nobody ever heard from them again. The Norwegian part is the most fun, my kids now think we're Vikings and my son has been walking around the house with a pot lid as a shield. My husband says he's twenty percent pirate, which isn't how it works, but I've stopped correcting him.

I'm at the grocery store and I just ran into my old college roommate, Jess, who I haven't seen in fifteen years. She lives two towns over now, has three boys, and works as a pharmacist at the CVS on Route 9. We stood in the cereal aisle for twenty minutes. She said we should get the families together for a barbecue next summer. I hope we actually do. We were so close, and then life just happened. She hasn't changed at all, she still laughs exactly the same way, like a seal. We used to stay up until three in the morning in our dorm room at Penn State eating ramen and talking about who we were going to be. Neither of us became a famous novelist, but we both made it out okay.

Okay so the tooth fairy situation in this house has gotten out of control. Charlotte lost her first tooth last night and got five dollars because my husband didn't have anything smaller. Now her brother is telling everyone at school the rate is five bucks and two other parents texted me asking what we pay. What's the normal amount these days? When I was a kid it was a quarter. And my mother-in-law apparently sends the kids two dollar bills for every tooth, so now there's a whole secondary market going on in this house. Charlotte is already wiggling the next one. She asked me if teeth are worth more if you clean them first. I'm raising a little capitalist.

I volunteered at the food pantry this morning with my teenage son, which I'd been trying to get him to do for months. He complained the whole drive there and then ended up being the one who stayed late to help a lady carry her boxes to the bus stop. Her name was Mrs. Pham, and she told him he reminded her of her grandson. On the drive home he asked if we could go back next month. I didn't say anything because I didn't want to ruin it, but I was so proud.

Can you text my wife and tell her I'm running about twenty minutes late? The traffic on 287 is backed up past the bridge because of some accident, and I'm just crawling along here. I was supposed to pick up the dry cleaning too but that's not happening tonight.

I swear Mondays at the clinic are the worst. We had three walk-ins before eight, the printer jammed, and Dr. Patel was forty minutes late because his kid threw up in the car. I ate lunch standing up at two in the afternoon. I'm driving home now and I'm just going to sit in the driveway for ten minutes before I go inside. And then my sister called on my break to ask if I can host Christmas this year because her kitchen is getting redone. I said I'd think about it, which she knows means yes. I'm already counting chairs in my head. We'd need at least fourteen, and I have nine.

Should we get a second car or keep sharing one? I take the bus to work most days, but my wife needs it for the kids' stuff, and on Thursdays when I have the late client meeting it's a mess. A used Corolla is probably twelve to fifteen thousand. Insurance would go up maybe sixty a month. I'm not sure it's worth it. I could also just do one of those car share memberships for the Thursday thing, I think it's like fifteen dollars an hour. My coworker Deshawn does that and he swears by it. But then there's also the summer when the kids are home and my wife takes them everywhere, so maybe I'd need it more then.

Note to self: Lucas has the peanut allergy, not Leo. The two boys from Ava's class are always together and I keep mixing them up. Lucas is the one with the red glasses. I was about to give Lucas a peanut butter cookie at the playdate today and his mom grabbed it out of my hand. I felt terrible. I'm never going to mix that up again. His mom was really gracious about it, she said it happens all the time, but I could tell she was rattled. I'm going to start asking every parent about allergies before kids come over, not just assuming I'll remember. It's too important to wing it.

what should I get my father-in-law for his seventieth he likes fly fishing and old westerns and he already has like every gadget and he always says don't get me anything which is useless information last year I got him a fancy cooler and he still uses the old styrofoam one

I really should write down what the electrician said about the panel, but basically he said our breaker box is a Federal Pacific, which apparently is known for not tripping when it should, and replacing it is about twenty-two hundred. He said it's not an emergency but don't wait years. He's booked through January. He also mentioned that the outlet in the garage isn't a GFCI, which apparently it's supposed to be by code, so that's another hundred and fifty. I asked whether that panel was a fire risk, and he gave me this look and said, let's just say I wouldn't put it off. Great. Very comforting.

Let me just talk through this budget thing for a minute. Our mortgage is eighteen fifty, car payment is three twenty, daycare is fourteen hundred, groceries are running about nine hundred for the five of us, and utilities are around three hundred. My take-home is about fifty-two hundred and my husband's is about forty-one hundred. So we're technically fine, but there's barely anything left after the credit card and the kids' activities. I feel like we make decent money and still somehow never get ahead. I'm not asking for anything specific, I just needed to say the numbers out loud.

I remember my grandpa used to say you can tell a good mechanic by how clean his hands are at the end of the day, because the good ones don't waste motion. I thought about that today at the shop when the new kid, Marcus, came out of the bay spotless after a full brake job. He's nineteen and already better than half the guys there. I think he's going to be something. I told Marcus about it at lunch and he just shrugged and said his dad taught him that. Kid doesn't even know how good he is yet. I'm going to put his name in for the apprenticeship program at the dealership, they only take two people a year, and I think he'd be a lock.

Do you remember what I told you the kids' shoe sizes were? I'm at Target and there's a huge sale on winter boots and I'm blanking on whether Noah is a twelve or a thirteen now. The sale ends today and the line for the fitting guy is about ten people deep.

Why do cats knock things off tables? Like is it actually a hunting thing or are they just jerks? Pepper pushed my coffee mug off the counter this morning while looking me dead in the eye. She's done it three days in a row now and I'm out of mugs.

so last night my husband and I were talking about whether we should do Christmas at our house this year or go to his parents in Ohio and his mom already assumed we're coming because we did Thanksgiving with my side but our oldest is home from college for only ten days and she wants to see her friends here and driving eleven hours with the dog is honestly not fun and his sister is also going to Ohio with her kids and they haven't seen their cousins in a year so I feel like I'm the bad guy no matter what I choose and maybe the answer is to go for three days and then come back but that's twenty two hours of driving for three days which seems crazy

Okay I'm just going to vent for a second. My brother-in-law Gary borrowed the pressure washer in August and I asked for it back three times now and every time he says he'll drop it off this weekend and he never does. And now I need it for the deck before we stain it, and the stain is already sitting in the garage, two gallons of cedar tone that cost me ninety bucks. I don't want to make it a big thing at Thanksgiving but I'm about to.

I wonder how many hours a week I spend in the car driving kids around. Let's see. School drop-off and pickup is about an hour a day. Then soccer Tuesdays and Thursdays is forty minutes round trip, and violin on Wednesdays is another thirty. Saturday games could be anywhere. So it's probably nine or ten hours a week. That's a part-time job. And that's not counting the grocery store or the times someone forgets their water bottle and I have to drive back. My husband does mornings twice a week, which helps. But honestly some of my best conversations with my teenager happen in the car, because she doesn't have to look at me. So I guess it's not all wasted.

Do you think it's weird that I still keep every birthday card my kids have made me? I have a shoebox in the closet with like a hundred of them. Some are just scribbles. Some say "I love you mom" with three backwards letters. I can't throw any of them out. My husband says we're going to need a second shoebox by the time the youngest is in middle school, and he's probably right. My mom did the same thing with mine, and when she gave me the box on my wedding day I sat on the floor of the hotel room and read every single one. I guess that's why I can't let go of them. Someday my kids will think it's embarrassing, and then someday after that they won't.

You know, my mom used to keep a little notebook in her purse with everyone's sizes and birthdays and what they wanted for Christmas. She'd pull it out at the mall and just know. I always thought it was so old-fashioned, but now I have four kids and I get it completely. I don't have her system though. I have a hundred screenshots and no idea where any of them are. Last Christmas I bought my son the same Lego set he already had, because I forgot he got it for his birthday from his uncle. He was nice about it, but he definitely noticed.
